news.story_lead: Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October 2026 - Published 6 hours ago Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free. news.full_article_text: Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October 2026 - Published 6 hours ago Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free. It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi. He had contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in May. His mother also subsequently died. Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation. "Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak. "This is an encouraging moment for Kenya and for Africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X. - What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? Published 15 September Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October. All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission. Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers. Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday. Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over. The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown. Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries. Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams. The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country. In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens. Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings. The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries. Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June. But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE. The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures. Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August. news.headline: Gurugram bans coal, wood-fired tandoors at hotels and eateries under revised GRAP norms to curb pollution
news.story_lead: Gurugram bans coal, wood-fired tandoors at hotels and eateries under revised GRAP norms to curb pollution Under the revised provisions of the GRAP issued by the CAQM, only equipment powered by electricity, gas, or other approved clean fuels may now be used. District Magistrate and Gurugram Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh has issued orders to prohibit the use of coal and wood as fuel in tandoors at all hotels, restaurants, and open-air eateries across the district in an effort to combat air pollution. Under the revised provisions of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) issued by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), only equipment powered by electricity, gas, or other approved clean fuels may now be used in these establishments.

In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger". "These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook. Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected. "As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said. Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated. "Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said. Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected. The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools. The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project. Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals. Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption. Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in. "The text seemed almost comical," said Barrella, "it was like a message from Martians: 'We have come to annihilate you.' I even had a bit of a laugh." Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home. Some 280 school head teachers had already received threats in recent days, according to Italian reports. In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report". news.full_article_text: RBI issues domestic transfer norms; walk-in customers can send up to ₹50k The framework for Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) was introduced in order to facilitate small-value fund transfers through formal banking channels. Walk-in customers at bank branches can utilise the cash pay-in service to remit funds up to ₹ 50,000 directly to a beneficiary's bank account through NEFT, the Reserve Bank said on Wednesday. With a view to harmonising and consolidating the extant instructions relating to Domestic Money Transfer (DMT), the central bank has issued the Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026. The framework for Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) was introduced in order to facilitate small-value fund transfers through formal banking channels, particularly for persons, including migrant workers, who lack access to such channels due to lack of proof of identity/address. "A walk-in customer at a bank branch can remit funds up to ₹ 50,000 to the bank account of a beneficiary through NEFT," said the RBI's latest Directions, which came into effect from Wednesday. Banks are also permitted to allow such customers to transfer funds to a bank account of a beneficiary through Business Correspondents (BCs) and ATMs up to a maximum amount of ₹ 5,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of ₹ 25,000 per remitter. RBI further said banks are permitted to provide services, which facilitate transfer of funds from the accounts of their customers for delivery in cash to the recipients not having bank accounts at an ATM or through an agent appointed as Business Correspondent, or through any other authorised payment channels. On payment of amounts transferred from a bank account (Cash Pay-out Service), banks are permitted to provide services which facilitate transfer of funds from the accounts of their customers for delivery in cash to the recipients not having bank accounts at an ATM or through an agent appointed as Business Correspondent, or through any other authorised payment channels. "The maximum amount that may be transferred under the Cash Pay-out Service shall be ₹ 10,000 per transaction, subject to an overall monthly ceiling of ₹ 25,000 per beneficiary," the RBI said. ### मुख्य विषय क्षेत्र

- **विज्ञान एवं प्रौद्योगिकी विकास:** पूछताछ सत्र तकनीकी अपनाने, वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान और नवाचार-संचालित विकास को बढ़ावा देने के लिए आवश्यक व्यावहारिक नीतिगत हस्तक्षेपों पर केंद्रित था।
- **वित्तीय नीति एवं शासन:** सत्र में क्षेत्र-विशिष्ट विकास उद्देश्यों का समर्थन करने के लिए वित्तीय प्रबंधन और आर्थिक नीति के कार्यान्वयन पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया गया।

सांसदों ने जोर दिया कि अनुसंधान वित्तपोषण, प्रौद्योगिकी हस्तांतरण और समग्र क्षेत्र शासन में मौजूदा बाधाओं को दूर करने के लिए कार्रवाई योग्य रणनीतियाँ आवश्यक हैं।

विधायकों ने जिम्मेदार विभागीय प्रमुखों से ठोस नीतिगत समाधान की मांग की।
सत्र में तकनीकी अनुसंधान और वित्तीय नीति में व्यावहारिक परिणामों की आवश्यकता पर जोर दिया गया।
